counterparts_needing_dossiers.name: Dunoding (Welsh kingdom of Eifionydd and Ardudwy)

problems: Powys ends 1160 (infobox, Madog page) but Cliopatria's Powys Fadog and Wenwynwyn start 1169: years 1161-1168 are empty unless the successors start in 1160 or Powys's end is moved to 1168.
Hwicce ends 628 but the page keeps a Mercian client sub-kingdom to the 780s: the Mercia dossier must carry vassal_start / vassal_end with counterpart 'hwicce' (628..c. 780s) or the land is blank.
One-year overlaps with successors' first Cliopatria shapes: Bernicia 634 (Northumbria), Dumnonia 710 (Cornwall, Wessex), Hwicce 628 (Mercia); successors should win in those years.

Powys new keyframes 900-910 and 1063-1084 overlap Cliopatria's Seisyllwg and Gwynedd shapes (Gwynedd 1066-1084 is 10,721 km2 and contains Powys): the Gwynedd and Seisyllwg dossiers must say who holds the land.

Cliopatria row 'Kingdom of Dunoting' carries Wikipedia 'Dunoding' and Wikidata Q2264840, which belong to the Welsh kingdom; the shape is in the Yorkshire Dales. The dossier sets wikipedia to null and keeps the Q-id as given.
The Kingdom of Powys row was not split: the pages show one continuing kingdom and Cliopatria's gaps are periods of absorption (handled as events and two new keyframes).

WebFetch returns a model's answer over the page, not the page text: quotes in notes are as returned, and several requested items came back 'not present'; sources_total is 30 entries (24 distinct pages, some shared by several dossiers).

Page budget: Powys 9 of 9, Rheged 5 of 5, Hwicce 4 of 5, Dumnonia 2 of 2; Bernicia (6 cited) and Dunoting (3, one the wrong state, one failed) exceed their 1-2 because pages opened for neighbours were also cited.
